ground_truth.title: Best Electric Cars for the Money in 2026
ground_truth.author: Emmet White
ground_truth.main_content:
EVs can be a mixed bag when it comes to value. These electric cars deliver the most bang for your buck.

The Manufacturers

Cars are more expensive than ever. That's doubly true for electric cars, many of which routinely retail for over six figures. Despite that, there are a still a handful of great EVs that cost a lot less that provide good value for money. These are our favorite electric cars for those who are shopping with a more reasonable budget—with one highly affordable honorable mention at the end. More Car Rankings: Best Electric Trucks | Best Electric SUVs | Best Electric Sports Cars | Best Luxury Electric Cars | Best Electric Cars

1

2026 Hyundai Ioniq 5

Base price: $36,600
EPA-rated range: 245–318 miles

While its larger and less aerodynamic shape means that the Hyundai Ioniq 5 SUV doesn't have the outright range performance of its Ioniq 6 sedan sibling, it offers a similarly pleasant driving experience and impressive fast-charging capability. In base form, it manages to stay well under $40,000. Plus, we love how it looks, especially in the newly launched, off-road focused XRT trim. If performance is what you’re after, the high-performance Ioniq 5 N offers over 600 horsepower, a raucous fake paddle shifting transmission feature, and superb handling.

Tested: Hyundai Ioniq 5 XRT

2

2026 Nissan Leaf

Base price: $31,495
EPA-rated range: 256–303 miles

The Nissan Leaf was a pioneer among electric vehicles when it first launched in 2010, and it is now on its third generation. The makeover was long overdue, and the newest Leaf boasts stylish looks, competitive range, and an upscale interior. Plus, Nissan has managed to keep it affordable, too. Nissan currently offers a base model S+ trim at $31,495, but there is reportedly an even more affordable S trim on the way with an estimated price tag of well under $30,000.

Tested: 2026 Nissan Leaf Looks Better, Goes Farther

3

2026 Tesla Model 3

Tesla

Base price: $38,630
EPA-rated range: 309–363 miles

Say what you will about Tesla, but there's a reason the company's most affordable model, the Model 3, is a hit. Not only is it fun to drive, but it's also makes for a pleasant daily driver that can go pretty far on a single charge. An updated version recently went on sale with new front- and rear-end designs and numerous interior upgrades. The Performance version is legitimately quick and fun to drive, if you're willing to spend a little extra.

Tested: Tesla Model 3 Performance

4

2025 Hyundai Ioniq 6

Mike Austin

Base price: $39,095
EPA-rated range: 240–361 miles

The Hyundai Ioniq 6 is the Korean automaker's attempt to do more with less. The streamliner-style sedan is able to squeeze a respectable 361 miles of range out of its battery thanks to clever engineering and aerodynamics. And the Standard Range version with a smaller 53.0-kW battery pack starts at under $40,000. If you choose to spend a bit more on the SE Long Range model, starting at $44,045, it's among the longest-range EVs you can buy for any price. Hyundai is bringing a performance-oriented Ioniq 6 N to the U.S. soon, but we're not sure if the refreshed version of the standard Ioniq 6 will make it to our shores, so your best bet is to buy a leftover 2025 model.

Tested: The Hyundai Ioniq 6 Is Comfortably Weird

5

2026 Ford Mustang Mach-E

Ford

Base price: $39,490
EPA-rated range: 265–320 miles

It may not be a real Mustang, but the Ford Mustang Mach-E is an excellent EV crossover with handsome looks and competitive range. A low center of gravity and good suspension tuning means the Mach-E won't let you down on your favorite set of twisty roads, and the Mach-E Rally (pictured) excels off the beaten path, too. First launched in 2021, the Mach-E has become a staple of the EV market and Ford has worked to make small updates each year that keep it fresh.

The Mach-E Rally Proves EVs Can Deliver Huge Fun

6

2025 Kia EV6

Will Sabel Courtney

Base price: $44,395
EPA-rated range: 231–319 miles

The Kia EV6 is an electric hatchback we’re quite fond of. While it has climbed in price, the EV6 is capable of over 300 miles of range and is great to drive. It shares its platform with the Hyundai Ioniq lineup and offers the same fast-charging capability. Plus, it is also available in high-performance EV6 GT form with 641 horsepower.

Tested: The Kia EV6 Makes Life Simpler for the Tesla Convert

7

2026 Kia EV9

Kia

Base price: $56,545
EPA-rated range: 230–304 miles

Kia’s EV9 was one of the first three-row electric SUVs, but its appeal goes well beyond its cargo and passenger capacity. Handsome, boxy styling and impressive acceleration make the Kia EV9 a well-rounded family hauler. Both RWD and AWD versions are available, and the Kia’s DC fast-charging speeds are impressive, too. Plus, the adoption of a NACS charging port for 2026 opens up a new realm of charger availability.

Sadly, the Sporty GT Version Is Delayed

8

2026 Cadillac Lyriq

Base price: $60,995
EPA-rated range: 285–314 miles

Cadillac has worked hard to be taken seriously in the luxury segment, and the Lyriq has proven itself as an excellent choice for those looking for a slick, comfortable, good-looking electric crossover that can go over 300 miles before needing a recharge. It's significantly cheaper than many of its competitors too, including the BMW iX and Audi Q8 e-tron. Plus, a new V-series Lyriq offers 615 horsepower.

Tested: 2026 Cadillac Lyriq-V

9

2026 Rivian R1T

Rivian

Base price: $74,885
EPA-rated range: 258-420 miles

The electric pickup truck segment grew significantly over the last five years, as battery-powered models from Ford, Chevrolet, and Tesla all arrived. But Rivian has been in the game from the very beginning, first offering its R1T in 2021. With dual-, tri-, and quad-motor setups available, the R1T has a flavor for every kind of buyer. It’s certainly not affordable, but the competency and value of its lower-end, dual-motor versions is hard to ignore.

The Rivian R1T Quad-Motor Is Calculated Excess

10

Honorable Mention: 2027 Chevrolet Bolt EV

Chevy

Base price: $28,995
Estimated range: 255 miles

The Bolt was one of the best-value EVs out there for many years, and it's back by popular demand for 2027 after Chevrolet previously axed the model in 2023. Yep, Chevrolet will be building the Bolt again, this time offering faster charging and an improved battery pack. The 2027 Bolt will still start at under $30,000, which is an impressive feat in today's market, and will be offered in LT and RS trim levels. A front-mounted electric motor delivers 210 horsepower, and range is claimed at around 255 miles. We'll know more when the updated Bolt goes on sale at some point this year.

Chevy Is Planning a 'Family" of Bolt-Like Affordable EVs
